chapter: Picnics, lake resorts and lawn parties
title: Picnics at the fairground
summary: Picnics featured bands, dancing, food, drink and rides; Bailey spent four dollars on rides.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Do you remember many picnics when you were young? Did they give picnics in the country?
Oh yeah, at the fairground. That's where all the picnic was. Right out the fairground. Not a good place. Entertainment. What would they do at a picnic? Dancing, playing the music.
Well, how would they dance? Would they spread anything on the ground? No, they're dancing.
It's a big open place. Never been in that fairground?
Well, no, I don't know the place. Or the race.

Yeah, yeah. On the ground. College used to have that more than the white folks today one time. In my round, 1825. From 18 to 25, it was all a picnic. See all them holidays like old soldier did. I was labor day. And art fella day. There was every year a parade be coming. There was about five or six different parades. That's all I used to go to the fairground. That's the biggest place to hold the people them days. Fairground.
Well, how many bands would they have?

Oh, they would have two. They have a Sedaton band. You know, a Selen Matters band. And a Ragtime band be out in the field on the platform. You know, we'd be out there dancing. That's the Ragtime band. Nothing but drags. But the other ones, all that slow drag. And everything is out there shaking and thick. Yeah. Oh, that was something that's fairground. Yeah, that's fairground.
Would they drink much at the picnic?
See, I wouldn't go to work that day just to go to picnic. Better go sometime, go in the evening. I'll come back till 2, 3 o'clock in the morning.
Mostly picnic being for the children that day, but at nighttime for the big people. And they stay open from 8 to 4 o'clock in the morning, picnic all night.

Oh, yeah, eating and drinking. Plenty of eating. Plenty of eating, plenty of drinking. Plenty of entertainment they had. That's why I first learned, rode automobile. Cost me about $4 one evening. That's the road automobile of my life. Cost me $4. Diamond ride. Right around. That's a diamond ride. I would meet a girl. I wouldn't know her something. I'd treat her. That's a right ride. Yeah.

Yeah, you don't ride too far. No. It's a ride they give you. Yeah. But we're so glad. We didn't know what cars were. We were riding an automobile every day. They had flying horses and all that. All kind of entertainment. Plenty of music, nice music.
